div.span: They are not alternatives. DNS decides once, for a whole TTL, and never learns that a server stopped answering; the client keeps the dead address until the entry expires.
The load balancer decides on every request and tests each backend continuously, so a failure costs seconds. In practice DNS picks the Region and the balancer picks the server.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 51px; margin-left: 1313px;

div.span: - A normal DNS query. The zone holds three A records for the same name, which is what round robin is: three answers, handed out in turn.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 145px; margin-left: 1313px;

div.span: - Nothing in this exchange tests whether the servers are alive. The name server reads its zone file and returns what is written there, down or not.

div.b: The failure lands on the client

div.span: - One third of the clients get the address of the dead server, and they keep using it for the rest of the TTL. Lowering the TTL shortens the outage but multiplies the queries; it never removes it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 349px; margin-left: 1313px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;
display: inline-block; font-size: 22px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #121212); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 546px; height: 1px; padding-top: 331px; margin-left: 1366px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.b: With a balancer the client sees one address

div.span: - The name resolves to the balancer, so the client never holds a backend address and has nothing stale to cache.

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;

div.b: The health check removes the server

div.span: - The balancer probes every backend every few seconds. A backend that fails is taken out of the pool, and put back automatically once it answers again.

div.span: - Because the balancer sits in the request path it can weigh real load, keep a session on one server, and route on the URL or a header. DNS sees none of that.

div.span: - Grey solid: a request. Green dashed: the DNS answer and its TTL.
- Red dashed: the path to a server that is not answering. On the left it is still used; on the right it is already cut.
